teachingQuestion: How does an owner turn asset context into a useful classification?
focalInsight: Classification is a business and risk decision that must lead to handling rules.
title: From asset context to handling rule
caption: Inventory and ownership precede classification; classification becomes useful only when it drives controls.

nodes.label: Assess value, sensitivity, criticality, privacy, and obligations
Apply handling, access, retention, and disposal rules
Review when purpose, content, or risk changes

altSummary: A six-step loop identifies an asset, assigns owner and custodian, assesses value and sensitivity, selects a classification, applies handling rules, and reviews the decision when context changes.
textFallback: Start by identifying the information, copies, systems, and dependencies. Assign an accountable owner and an operating custodian. The owner assesses value, sensitivity, criticality, privacy, and obligations, then selects a classification. That label drives handling, access, retention, and disposal rules. Reassess when the purpose, content, ownership, or risk changes.
